read.passage: Last year, Reem left her science project to the last minute. The night before the deadline, her laptop crashed, and she lost everything. 'I could kick myself,' she says. 'I should have saved my work online.' She had to start again and finished at three in the morning. In hindsight, Reem thinks the problem was a blessing in disguise. Her teacher noticed how tired she was and walked her through a better way to plan her work, step by step. Now Reem uses a planner app, which she says has been a game changer. 'If you ask me, every student should try it,' she says. 'It's easier than it sounds, and you'll learn it in no time.'

qs.q: What should Reem have done, according to her?
qs.cando: Can understand personal stories and explanations in detail.

qs.q: Why does Reem call the problem a blessing in disguise?
options: She didn't have to finish the project.
She got a better mark than before.
Her teacher taught her a better way to plan.
qs.cando: Can understand personal stories and explanations in detail.

qs.q: What does Reem recommend to other students?

read2.passage: When Yazeed was twelve, his bike broke and his family couldn't afford to repair it. Instead of giving up, he watched online videos and taught himself to fix it. Soon, neighbours started bringing him their bikes. 'At first I made loads of mistakes,' he admits. 'I should have asked for help sooner, but I was too proud.' Now sixteen, Yazeed runs a small repair workshop in his family's garage every weekend. He charges low prices and gives free repairs to younger children. His dream is to open a proper shop one day. 'If I'd known how much I'd enjoy it, I'd have started even earlier,' he says.

qs.q: Why did Yazeed learn to fix bikes?
options: His school had a bike club.
His family couldn't pay for the repair.
qs.cando: Can understand personal stories and explanations in detail.
